title: 46,XY Differences of Sex Development: Androgen Insensitivity, 5-ARD and Gonadectomy Timing
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Adrenal Cortex, CAH and Differences of Sex Development

steps.say: Differences of sex development in 46,XY infants are systematically classified by embryological mechanisms.
steps.tx: Execute diagnostic evaluation under the **46,XY DSD diagnostic classification** framework. 46,XY DSD results from impaired testis development (SRY/SOX9 gonadal dysgenesis), impaired androgen synthesis (CYP17A1, HSD17B3), or impaired androgen action (androgen receptor or 5-alpha-reductase-2 defects). Evaluation mandates chromosomal karyotyping, extensive imaging of internal pelvic anatomy, and targeted molecular panel sequencing.

steps.say: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome produces a phenotypic female with absent internal Müllerian structures.
steps.tx: Recognize the **Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS) phenotype** in phenotypic adolescent females. CAIS is an X-linked recessive androgen receptor (AR) mutation presenting with completely normal female external genitalia, blind-ending vagina, absent uterus/fallopian tubes (due to normal Sertoli anti-Müllerian hormone AMH), and bilateral intra-abdominal testes.

vis.title: Endocrine and Anatomical Hallmarks of CAIS
rows: Absent uterus, fallopian tubes & upper vagina
Normal Sertoli cell secretion of AMH

steps.say: Gonadectomy is deferred until after spontaneous puberty to permit natural estrogen production through aromatization.
steps.tx: Determine appropriate **Post-pubertal gonadectomy timing in CAIS** to maximize psychosexual and skeletal development. In CAIS, bilateral gonadectomy is safely deferred until late adolescence (after completion of spontaneous female puberty driven by aromatization of endogenous testicular androgens), with malignancy risk < 2-5% before age 20.

left.title: Pre-Pubertal Gonadectomy
points: Requires artificial exogenous pubertal induction with estrogen
Often results in sub-optimal spontaneous breast contour

right.title: Post-Pubertal Gonadectomy (Preferred)
points: Permits natural spontaneous thelarche via endogenous aromatization
Malignancy risk before age 20 remains exceptionally low (< 2-5%)
Requires bilateral gonadectomy after adult height attainment

steps.say: Partial androgen insensitivity presents with ambiguous genitalia and shows variable responsiveness to testosterone.
steps.tx: Evaluate the clinical spectrum of **Partial androgen insensitivity syndrome (PAIS)** across infancy and puberty. PAIS exhibits partial AR responsiveness, presenting with ambiguous genitalia (micropenis, bifid scrotum, perineoscrotal hypospadias) and gynecomastia at puberty; response to high-dose testosterone cypionate therapy is variable.

vis.title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Assessment in PAIS

steps.say: Deficiency of 5-alpha-reductase type 2 causes striking virilization at puberty due to the surge of testosterone.
steps.tx: Recognize the striking evolution of **5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency (SRD5A2)** from infancy to adolescence. Autosomal recessive SRD5A2 mutations impair dihydrotestosterone (DHT) synthesis, causing ambiguous genitalia at birth but dramatic virilization at puberty (phallic growth, muscle mass, voice deepening) due to testosterone surge. Longitudinal management requires meticulous follow-up to support psychosexual adjustment and optimize male phallic reconstruction where feasible.

vis.title: SRD5A2 Evolution: Birth vs Puberty
rows: Marked phallic enlargement, testicular descent, deepening voice
Absent prostate tissue, minimal facial and body hair

steps.say: An abnormally high ratio of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone after hCG stimulation confirms the diagnosis.
steps.tx: Measure the **Testosterone-to-DHT ratio diagnostic cutoff** following endocrine stimulation. Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) stimulation testing yields an abnormally elevated serum testosterone-to-DHT ratio (> 20-30:1) in 5-alpha-reductase deficiency compared to normal (< 10:1), distinguishing SRD5A2 deficiency from partial androgen insensitivity. Meticulous evaluation prevents misdiagnosis and directs appropriate surgical timing.

left.title: 5-Alpha-Reductase Deficiency
points: Marked rise in serum testosterone post-hCG

right.title: Partial Androgen Insensitivity (PAIS)
points: Parallel rise in both testosterone and DHT
Impaired end-organ AR responsiveness despite high DHT

steps.say: Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome occurs in phenotypically normal males found to have uterine structures.
steps.tx: Identify the anatomical findings of **Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome (PMDS)** during pediatric groin surgery. PMDS is caused by mutations in AMH or AMHR2, presenting in phenotypically normal 46,XY males who are found to have uterus and fallopian tubes during surgery for inguinal hernia (hernia uteri inguinalis) or cryptorchidism.

vis.title: Surgical Presentation of PMDS

nodes.label: Confirm AMH or AMHR2 Genetic Mutation

edges: Avoid damage to vas deferens embedded in uterine wall

steps.say: Dysgenetic intra-abdominal gonads carry high risk of malignant degeneration, requiring early surgical removal.
steps.tx: Establish surgical vigilance regarding the **Malignancy risk in dysgenetic gonads** in differences of sex development. In 46,XY partial gonadal dysgenesis with intra-abdominal gonads, the risk of gonadoblastoma and seminoma exceeds 30-50%, mandating early prophylactic laparoscopic gonadectomy upon diagnosis, in contrast to the lower risk in CAIS.

vis.title: Neoplastic Risk Stratification in 46,XY DSD
rows: Early prophylactic bilateral gonadectomy at diagnosis
Deferred until completion of spontaneous puberty
